speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me specifically which antibiotic you were prescribed and for what infection?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood count is normal, which is a good start. Could you describe the appearance of the itchy rash and tell me if the joint pain is symmetrical or localized to specific joints?

REQUEST TEST: Erythromyeloblasts

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal erythromyeloblast count makes acute leukemia unlikely. Is the rash spreading quickly, and do you notice any specific joint swelling or warmth? REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ANA test results are coming back normal, which helps rule out lupus. Did you develop a rash shortly after starting the antibiotics, and are you currently taking any other medications or supplements?

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests
REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver_Function_Tests: NORMAL READINGS; Skin_Biopsy: Pending

speaker: Doctor
text:
The liver function tests are normal, and the skin biopsy is pending. Did the rash appear specifically on your cheeks or in a sun-exposed "butterfly" pattern, and do you have any eye redness or dry mouth symptoms?

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Clinical_Photography

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-induced urticarial vasculitis secondary to amoxicillin.
